newsitem.title: UK: U.S. drags global bonds lower in week -Salomon.
newsitem.headline: U.S. drags global bonds lower in week -Salomon.

text.p: Caution from Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan knocked U.S. bonds and took most other bond markets lower in the latest week, data from Salomon Brothers showed on Friday.
U.S. bonds fell 1.06 percent, the heaviest losers in the week. Overall, the World Government Bond Index fell 0.50 percent.

Treasuries slumped after Greenspan warned about inflation risks and the buoyant equity market in his semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to Congress, and hinted at the possibility of a rise in interest rates.
"We may decide to move ... before you see actual evidences of real inflation emerging," Greenspan said.
The dollar bloc also felt the impact of Greenspan's words. Australian bonds lost 0.91 percent in Australian dollar terms, while Canadian bonds fell 0.85 percent.
European bonds struggled to free themselves from the U.S. downturn. Bunds fell 0.25 percent in marks, gilts dropped 0.29 percent in pounds and French bonds lost 0.38 percent in francs.
Dutch bonds lost 0.36 percent in guilders in a week when the Dutch central bank raised rates.
Italian bonds were one of the few gainers on the week, pushing up 0.08 percent in lira terms. Swiss bonds made the largest gains, at a rise of 0.21 percent in francs.
In dollar terms, Canadian bonds were the worst performers, sliding 1.57 percent.

Other bond markets benefited from the weaker dollar. JGBs jumped 1.61 percent in dollars, despite losing 0.04 percent in yen, as fears of Japanese corporate repatriation of funds at year-end weighed on the greenback.
Gilts drove 1.04 percent higher in dollars, and the index made an overall loss of only 0.02 percent in dollar terms.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
